items.title: Start with the problem
items.body: Briefs arrive as feature requests. I use interviews and research to work out what people actually need, then write it down as one sentence the team can agree on.

items.title: Model the data first
items.body: I settle the objects and their states — what a booking or a complaint really is — before designing screens. Getting this wrong is expensive to undo later.

items.title: Set the structure
items.body: One shell, one navigation model, one pattern for list, record and edit. After that, a new screen only needs its content described.

items.title: Design every state
items.body: Empty, loading, partial, failed, offline, overloaded. I draw components in the conditions they will actually meet, including a mid-range phone on a bad connection.

items.title: Test and revise
items.body: Usability sessions and preference tests. When people struggle with something, I change it, even when I preferred the earlier version.

items.title: Hand off with the reasoning
items.body: Specs, tokens and component states, with the reason for each decision written next to the frame it belongs to.
